newsitem.title: UK: Sterling/mark corrects lower, cable flounders.
newsitem.headline: Sterling/mark corrects lower, cable flounders.

text.p: Sterling softened against the mark throughout the European session as operators locked in profits after Tuesday's rise to a 53-month peak, dropping nearly two pfennigs from the day's high.
Traders, however, were not overly concerned.

"The pound does look weak at this precise moment as far as today's moves are concerned, but you have to take into consideration how strong it's been the past couple of days," said one trader at a Japanese bank here.
Sterling was slightly above its day's low at 2.7560/70 marks at 1553 GMT against 2.7615/25 in late Europe on Tuesday.

The only event of note as far as sterling was concerned was the monthly monetary meeting between UK Chancellor Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England governor Eddie George, but this resulted in key interest rates staying on hold, as expected.
The Bank of England set its repo rate at an unchanged 6.0 percent in its routine money market operation after the meeting.

"Sterling failed to break substantially through that level (of 2.77 marks) which had been seen as a key level... If we'd seen it going through to, say, 2.7750 (marks) then we would have seen continued buying coming through," said Deborah Read, economic advisor at BankAmerica here.
Sterling/mark hit a high of 2.7700 on Tuesday.
The pound was also struggling against the dollar, pressured by the U.S. currency's continued strength against the mark. Cable fell to $1.6081/85 from late Tuesday's $1.6161/68.

"There's a tremendous support level for cable at $1.60, and if breaks below that it could trigger a big slide. And when a target like that comes into sight, the market's inclined to chase and test it," the Japanese bank dealer said.
Sterling/yen, meanwhile, weakened in line with a drop in mark/yen. Sterling was at 195.60/83 yen against late Tuesday's level of 197.02. -- Chizu Nomiyama +44-171-542-6721
